I need to evaluate the claim that Bodhidharma was called "The Blue-Eyed Barbarian" in Chinese texts.

Bodhidharma was indeed a Buddhist monk who lived around the 5th-6th century CE and is credited with bringing Chan (Zen) Buddhism to China. Historical and legendary accounts describe him as coming from either India or Persia, and Chinese texts do refer to him with various epithets.

The term "blue-eyed barbarian" (碧眼胡 or similar variants) appears in Chinese Chan/Zen literature in reference to Bodhidharma. The "barbarian" (胡) designation was commonly used for foreigners from the west, and the "blue-eyed" descriptor aligns with accounts of his foreign appearance. This epithet is well-documented in Chan Buddhist texts and literature.
